manifest.hypothesis: narrowed on 2026-10-10 (scope change decided by the coordinating head of work package LR; the remainder is the planned successor R014) from the successor to R011 that R013 was when it was split out of R011 on 2026-10-08. R013 now carries two tiers. Tier 1, what the existing runtime can already be asked, reusing R011's fixtures: (a) dormant seeds: an expert retired before the authority or the input it rested on was revoked is not reactivated from that compromised seed (kinds: gate configuration, evaluator, training input, attestor); (b) transitive authority: a descendant (a Merge result, a Split result, a Reactivate generation) of a source admitted under an earlier epoch of the gate configuration or the evaluator is fenced when the authority is revoked, on the normal, reopen and compacted-restore paths; (c) superseded sources: a live descendant of a consumed source whose input or attestor is revoked after the source was consumed is fenced through the source edge; (d) in-flight calls racing the invalidation of the base model or of an adapter are cancelled at their next use and emit nothing after the event. Tier 2, a signed attestor mechanism built for this experiment (crates/ptr-runtime, expert/attestation.rs): an attestation is a record signed (Ed25519, strict verification) by an attestor key that the host registered under a gate grant with its epoch; it binds one proposal, one emitted artifact digest, the base model, the result experts and generations, one single-use training run id and the attestor at its epoch; the attestor, the run and the signature are input identities of the admitted expert's dependency block, so an attestor revocation is the existing compound input invalidation (terminal for the experts admitted under it, which are never readmitted and never a Reactivate seed), a new attestor epoch is a new input generation, and the run id is single-use because a record that names a run:{id} input in any role at any generation after an earlier record named it is refused (the rule lives in the shared dependency check, so replay re-checks it); admission with an attestation refuses an attestor the host never registered, a signature that does not verify, and a claim that names another proposal, artifact, base model or result, and a grant that requires attestation refuses an artifact-producing admission without one; the requirement is recorded with the admission, so a restart with a looser grant cannot admit an unattested artifact-producing record and a replay refuses one. What R013 carried before this narrowing and no longer carries, because it needs mechanisms that do not exist: trusted evaluators and attested manifests, an attestor-removing rotation, Birth with a source expert (upcycling), multi-cause readmission, hard-deny verifiers and verifier-set epochs, Split per-result gating and provenance references, the source-expert in-flight race and the verifier-set kind of the transitive and dormant families; these move, with their metrics and falsification text, to R014 (planned, no harness). These claims inherit R011's definitions (event mapping, verifier, direct append, route, input digest). The registry of attestor keys is host memory, not history (the host supplies it again at a restart and a replay against a registry that lacks a key refuses the record); the signature binds claims, not weights. No evidence is claimed: the experiment is planned.

Each coverage threshold is the plan's structural lower bound for one seed (every cell of the plan runs once per seed): an adversarial case is attempted at least once; each in-flight kind (base model, adapter) runs both triggers; each transitive-authority kind runs three forms on three paths; each dormant-seed kind runs on three paths with the control reactivation accepted in every cell; each superseded-source kind runs its forms on three paths; the attestation, run-reuse, requirement, revoked-attestor and quarantine cells run as many times as the plan lists them (a positive control is counted when the runtime accepts it). Falsified if any of: structural_inflight_outputs_after_invalidation > 0; routable_descendants_after_source_authority_revocation > 0; reactivations_from_compromised_seed_admitted > 0; compromised_reactivations_routable > 0; descendants_routable_after_superseded_source_revocation > 0; mismatched_attestation_admissions > 0; unattested_admissions > 0; untrusted_attestor_admissions > 0; self_trusted_attestor_admissions > 0; revoked_attestor_evidence_admissions > 0; attestor_quarantine_readmissions_admitted > 0; inflight_fallback_incomplete > 0; inflight_fallback_output_mismatches > 0; fence_set_mismatches > 0; bystanders_closed > 0; registry_replay_mismatches > 0; procedure_mismatches > 0; wrong_typed_refusals > 0; skipped_cells > 0; product_panics > 0. Definitions: a seed retired before an input or an attestor was revoked is compromised and any reactivation of it is owed a refusal, whatever block names it (revoked data is not laundered by retraining); a seed retired before an authority kind was revoked is compromised for evidence of the revoked authority, and a reactivation on evidence under the standing that replaced it is a re-evaluation (the positive control). An expert admitted under an attestor is fenced with the terminal cause InputRevoked when the attestor is revoked, so it is never readmitted and never a Reactivate seed. fence_set_mismatches, bystanders_closed, registry_replay_mismatches, procedure_mismatches, product_panics and the inflight_fallback_* counters are guards this experiment adds to the R013 text before its narrowing of 2026-10-10 (they were not in it); wrong_typed_refusals counts a refusal of an attempt with a typed error other than the one the case owes (a product contract violation, not a harness error), and skipped_cells counts the coverage prerequisites a run left unmet (a cell that did not run); every seed of the listed seeds must pass every criterion above. Thresholds are the plan's lower bounds, decided in this experiment's preregistration; they are not frozen.
